meta.title: Laterite to metal extraction
meta.subtitle: Winning nickel, cobalt and manganese from low-grade laterite ore by bioleaching.
meta.functionalUnit: 1 kg of recovered critical metal (Al + Mn + Ni + Co) from the Mn-oxide concentrate bioleach
meta.boundary: Cradle-to-gate. Starts at mined laterite ore arriving wet at the plant, ends at recovered metal in the bioleach liquor. Excludes mining itself and downstream refining.
meta.source: Reproduces standalone/laterite-lca-tea.html (Balance, Energy GWP-MnO w allocation, Energy GWP-MnO no-alloc, Energy and GWP-BFL and TEA-price MnO BFL worksheets).

notes.title: Mozley stream counted twice
notes.text: The Mn-oxide concentrate is worked out as attrition feed minus fines minus heavies (72 - 69 - 0.6 = 2.4 kg/h). The 1.7 kg/h sent to Mozley separation is never subtracted, so it is inside the concentrate as well as in its own stream and the attrition block puts out 73.7 kg/h from 72 kg/h in. The attrition energy uses a different remainder (72 - 69 - 1.7 = 1.3 kg/h) for the coarse size fraction. Both are kept exactly as the spreadsheet has them.

notes.title: Split fractions are frozen x/360 ratios
notes.text: Every size fraction is a fixed ratio of the feed taken from the 360 kg/h reference case (20/360, 268/360, 72/360, 69/360, 1.7/360, 0.6/360). Changing the feed scales every stream together; the split itself never moves and does not respond to ore properties.

notes.title: Cobalt recovery uses the silicon grade
notes.text: In both composition tables the cobalt recovery formula points one row down and multiplies the Co recovery (87.2% and 79.1%) by the Si wt% (0.4% and 1.0%) instead of the Co wt% (2.3% and 0.164%). The 'wt% used by recovery' column shows the grade actually applied; it is reproduced so that the graph matches the published numbers.

notes.title: Bioleach CAPEX size fed in t/h against a kg/h base
notes.text: Seven equipment rows are scaled on their feed in kg/h against a 33.5 t/h (33,500 kg/h) reference. The bioleaching row divides its feed by 1000 first (0.0224) and compares that with an 18.5 t/h reference written as 18,500, so its cost is scaled on a size ratio that is 1000 times too small.

notes.title: LCA is mass-allocated, TEA is not
notes.text: The climate footprint charges the Mn-oxide concentrate only with its mass share of each energy step (drying, crushing, attrition). The operating cost charges the whole coarse line plus the whole bulk-fine line, unallocated. The two panels therefore describe different systems.

notes.title: Co-product GWP divided equally by three
notes.text: The per-metal footprints for Mn, Ni and Co are the total concentrate GWP divided by each metal's recovered mass and then by 3, a flat equal split across three co-products that ignores aluminium and does not sum back to the total.

notes.title: Na2SO4 default is 0 on load, 60 after reset
notes.text: The dashboard's Na2SO4 field is 0 g/L when the page loads (the value the published numbers and the recorded baseline reflect) but its reset button sets it to 60 g/L. The graph uses 0 so that it matches the page as shown.

notes.title: Dry basis applied twice
notes.text: The feed entered is already dry, yet the bioleach volume, the metal recoveries and the BFL disk-milling energy multiply the concentrate and BFL flows by (1 - moisture) again. Only 1.8 of the 2.4 kg/h of concentrate is leached and recovered from.

notes.title: Manganese molar mass taken as 57
notes.text: The BFL manganese grade converts MnO to Mn with 57/(57+16); the true molar mass of Mn is 54.94.

stages.title: Mass balance
stages.tryIt: The size fractions are fixed ratios of the feed, so click the ore stream and change the throughput: everything scales together and the split never moves. Now raise the moisture from 25% to 40% — the dry flows are untouched, but look at what happens to the drying energy in the next step.

stages.title: Life cycle inventory
stages.tryIt: Drop the bioleach solid concentration from 50 to 20 g/L and re-run. More water per kilogram of ore means more slurry to heat, and the heat demand climbs sharply for no extra metal.

stages.title: Impact assessment
stages.tryIt: Look at which of the four contributors dominates. Then cut the FeSO₄ dose to the Mn oxide bioleach from 25 to 10 g/L and re-run to see how much of the footprint is one reagent.

stages.title: Capital cost
stages.tryIt: Every unit is scaled with the six-tenths rule from a 33.5 t/h reference plant. Multiply the ore feed by ten and watch capital rise by roughly six times, not ten — that gap is the economy of scale.

stages.title: Operating cost & revenue
stages.tryIt: Set the raw laterite price to zero, as if the ore were a mine waste stream rather than a purchased feed. For a low-grade resource that single assumption often decides the whole case.

stages.title: Profitability
stages.tryIt: Compare the break-even metal price against the $18.50/kg assumed. If break-even sits above the market price, the process needs either a richer ore or a cheaper feed.

scope.tryIt: This case has four saleable metals from one ore, so the functional unit lumps them together. Splitting the burden between co-products instead — allocation — would give four different numbers from exactly the same plant.

interpret.tryIt: Ore grade, moisture and feed price dominate here. Note that two of the three are properties of the deposit, not choices the designer gets to make.

o.label: O
o.source: Oxygen, used to convert the BFL oxide assays to metal grades.

ncl.label: NCL raw material (dry)
ncl.source: Balance L3. Dry mass of nickel-cobalt laterite ore fed to the plant.

moist.label: Moisture content
moist.source: Balance L12. Free water in the as-mined ore; all of it has to be evaporated.

ref_feed.label: Reference feed of the Balance sheet
ref_feed.source: Balance L3 basis (360 kg/h) from which every split fraction is taken.

solidc.label: Bioleach solid concentration
solidc.source: Balance O3. Pulp density in both bioleach reactors.

na2so4.label: Na₂SO₄ dose — BFL
na2so4.source: Balance O5. Reagent added to the bulk fine laterite bioleach.

feso4b.label: FeSO₄ dose — BFL
feso4b.source: Balance O6. Iron source for the bulk fine laterite bioleach.

feso4m.label: FeSO₄ dose — Mn oxides conc.
feso4m.source: Balance O7. Iron source for the Mn oxide concentrate bioleach; the dominant reagent burden.

rho_water.label: Water density
rho_water.source: Energy sheet B32: slurry is 1 kg/L.

attr_f80.label: Attrition feed size F80
attr_f80.source: Energy sheet B16: crushed ore at 20 mm.

coprod_n.label: Number of co-products sharing the GWP
coprod_n.source: Cells C43, C46, C47 divide by 3.

acc.label: Annual capital charge
acc.source: TEA B19. Fraction of total capital charged each operating year.

preag.label: Reagents price
preag.source: TEA D16. Blended across FeSO₄ and Na₂SO₄.

pmet.label: Critical metals price
pmet.source: TEA D24. Blended across the recovered metal streams.

plat.label: Raw laterite price
plat.source: TEA D23. Price of ore delivered to the plant.

plab.label: Labour cost
plab.source: TEA D21. Per worker per year.

indir_frac.label: Indirect fixed opex, fraction of annual capital charge

misc_frac.label: Miscellaneous opex, fraction of (indirect + labour + variable)

irr.label: Discount rate
irr.source: TEA B20. Rate used to discount future cash flows.

splits.label: Balance sheet split basis (flows at the 360 kg/h reference feed)

mnox_comp.label: Mn oxides concentrate — composition and bioleach recovery (Balance L14–M23)

rec_uses_si.label: Recovery formula points at the Si row (1 = yes)

bfl_comp.label: Bulk fine laterite — oxide assay, metal grade and bioleach recovery (Balance L25–M34)

rec_uses_si.label: Recovery formula points at the Si row (1 = yes)

capex.label: Capital cost estimation — six-tenths rule (TEA rows 4–11)

size_key.label: Size basis (1 wet ore, 2 dry ore, 3 BFL, 4 attrition feed, 5 Mozley feed, 6 bioleach feed in t/h)

mnox.label: Mn oxides concentrate
mnox.basis: Balance L11 = L7 - L8 - L10 (L9 not subtracted)

liquor_mn.label: Leach solution — Mn-ox concentrate
liquor_mn.basis: Energy sheet B29 = D30 × (1 - moist) × B2 / (D29 / 1000)

metal.label: Recovered metal — Mn-ox concentrate (Al + Mn + Ni + Co)

metal_bfl.label: Recovered metal — BFL (Al + Mn + Cr + Ni + Co)

residue.label: Leach residue and spent reagents
residue.expr: mnox + bfl_milled + feso4_mn + feso4_bfl + na2so4_bfl - metal - metal_bfl

mnox_dry.label: Mn-ox concentrate leached (dry basis applied again)

mnox_wt_rec.label: wt% used by the recovery formula

mnox_rec_kgh.label: kg/h recovered
mnox_rec_kgh.basis: Energy sheet B42–B47 = N × D30 × (1 - moist) × B2

bfl_wt.label: Metal wt% in BFL
bfl_wt.expr: if(isnull(row.ppm), row.oxide_pct * row.n_metal * row.mw_metal / (row.n_metal * row.mw_metal + row.n_oxygen * mw.o), row.ppm / 1e6)
bfl_wt.basis: Balance L25–L34: oxide assay × metal share of the oxide molar mass; ppm / 10⁴ for Ni and Co

bfl_wt_rec.label: wt% used by the recovery formula

attr_frac_coarse.label: Coarse remainder per kg NCL
attr_frac_coarse.basis: Energy sheet D20 = (L7 − L8 − L9) / L3

e_attr_spec.label: Attrition & wet sieving specific energy (PSD-weighted Bond)
e_attr_spec.expr: (bond(bwi_attr, attr_f80, attr_p80_mozl) * attr_frac_mozl + bond(bwi_attr, attr_f80, attr_p80_coarse) * attr_frac_coarse + bond(bwi_attr, attr_f80, attr_p80_fine) * attr_frac_fine) / 1000
e_attr_spec.basis: Energy sheet B16: Bond work from 20 mm to each fraction's P80, weighted by the fraction of NCL

e_mozl.label: Mozley separation energy
e_mozl.basis: Energy sheet B26 = D20 × D26 × 3.6/1000 × (1 − moist) × B2

ealloc.label: Electricity allocated to Mn-ox concentrate
ealloc.expr: q_oven * mnox / ncl_wet + (q_dry40 + e_crush) * mnox / ncl_dry + (e_attr + e_mozl) * mnox / bcl_attr
ealloc.basis: Energy sheet B27: each step's energy × mass share of the concentrate in that step's feed

q_bio_mn.label: Bioleach heating to 46 °C — Mn-ox concentrate
q_bio_mn.expr: liquor_mn / 1000 * ((rho_water - solidc) / 1000 * cp_w + solidc / 1000 * cp_s) * (t_bio - t_cold)

q_bio_bfl.label: Bioleach heating to 46 °C — BFL
q_bio_bfl.expr: liquor_bfl / 1000 * ((rho_water - solidc) / 1000 * cp_w + solidc / 1000 * cp_s) * (t_bio - t_cold)

noalloc_elec.label: Electricity — coarse line (unallocated)
noalloc_elec.expr: (q_oven + q_dry40 + e_crush) * bcl / ncl_dry + e_attr + e_mozl

crit_tpa.label: Critical metal streams to bioleach (Mn-ox conc. + BFL)

gwp_fe_fu.label: GWP per kg metal — ferrous sulfate

capex_size.label: Current size
capex_size.expr: row.size_key == 1 ? ncl_wet : row.size_key == 2 ? ncl_dry : row.size_key == 3 ? bfl : row.size_key == 4 ? bcl_attr : row.size_key == 5 ? bcl_mozl : (mnox + bfl_milled) / 1000
capex_size.basis: TEA column F; the bioleach row is (Mn-ox conc. + BFL) / 1000

capex_cost.label: Cost
capex_cost.expr: six_tenths(row.base_cost, row.size, row.base_size, row.n, row.cepci_base, cepci_now)
capex_cost.basis: TEA H4–H11: base × (size / base size)ⁿ × CEPCI_now / CEPCI_base

lab_opex.label: Labour cost-dependent opex
lab_opex.basis: TEA B29 = kt product × 23 jobs/kt × salary × 1.9

cum_npv.label: Cumulative NPV
cum_npv.basis: TEA column G, running sum of column F

msp.label: Break-even metal price (total cost ÷ product)
msp.basis: Annual cost per kg of critical metal stream

ore_closure.label: Ore balance closure (NCL dry → BFL + storage + attrition)

attr_closure.label: Attrition closure (fines + Mozley + heavies + Mn-ox concentrate)

lcia.method: Spreadsheet GWP factors (Energy GWP-MnO w allocation, column D)

categories.label: Global warming per kg metal recovered

lca.basis: Each energy step is charged to the Mn-oxide concentrate in proportion to its mass share of that step's feed (oven on wet feed, drying and crushing on dry feed, attrition and Mozley on attrition feed).

coproducts.basis: The concentrate GWP is divided by each metal's recovered mass and then by 3 across Mn, Ni and Co.

tea.basis: Operating cost charges the unallocated coarse line plus the whole bulk-fine line.

tornado_gwp.label: What moves the footprint per kg metal?

grid_feed_price.label: NPV against ore price and feed rate
